attempts.description: Tests the findings of Zhuang, Lemak, Sridhar and Nelson (2025) on dandiset 001177 and on the paper's Zenodo deposit (doi:10.5281/zenodo.15258978). The dandiset holds raw voltage, LFP and threshold crossings of the striatal recordings, without sorted or labelled units, so the electrophysiology claims are blocked. The delay discounting, rotarod, open field, histology and slice claims are tested on the Zenodo files, recounting every operant session from its raw log.

findings.statement: DANDI:001177 holds, for 18 mice and 56 sessions, the 30 kHz voltage, the 1 kHz LFP and per-electrode threshold crossings with their waveforms, which are the input to the paper's manual spike sorting. It holds none of what the paper's electrophysiology analysis used; sorted single units (54 files have none), their putative MSN class, their optical identification, the laser pulse times and the PPX injection time. None of the 14 electrophysiology findings (Figures 4, 6F-I, S5, S8) can be tested.

Two files (sub-E0 PPX day 4, sub-P4 PPX day 1) have a units table with spike times and unit names only. Even-numbered and odd-numbered units differ by about two orders of magnitude in spike count in E0, consistent with an unsorted and a sorted cluster per channel, but no column gives the channel, the sorted status, the MSN class or an optical label.

Three sessions have start times in 2025 (sub-H0-2 days 3 and 4, 2025-07-31 and 2025-07-30, out of day order; sub-H4-3 day 3, 2025-05-23) while the same mice's other days are from 2023, likely the conversion date.
The subject descriptions are mis-encoded ('1.5â€¯microliters', a UTF-8 narrow space decoded twice), and the genotype is written 'Drd1a-Cre' in sub-E0's PPX sessions and 'Drd1aCre' elsewhere.

In the paper's Zenodo deposit (doi:10.5281/zenodo.15258978), the PPX open field data of Figure S1E-F are absent; parkinsonian mouse E6 has baseline but no PPX or washout delay discounting sessions; and mCherry mouse R5.5, listed in the README, has no delay discounting file.

In the Zenodo deposit, no file gives each mouse's sex (Figure S2A-C cannot be tested); the open field files carry no injection time (25 of 26 A77636 files show a tracking gap at 20 min, taken as the injection); six A77636 and four CNO open field mice are in no group list of the README; and the SNc cell count workbook has no group column, so three of its 32 mice cannot be placed.

The deposit holds 2 to 5 baseline sessions per mouse (1 to 5 before the first drug session), and the Methods' stability rule (CV < 20% in 3 blocks over three sessions or in all blocks over two) finds a stable run in only 12 of 47 PPX mice among them. Which baseline sessions entered the figures is not stated; using all deposited baselines gives the paper's statistics closely (delay F = 38.15 against 38.53).

Not all sessions follow the Methods' task. The 2020 cohort of six control PPX mice (P1 to P7) ran delays of 0, 6, 12 and 18 s, as both its block labels and the measured reward delays show, and 30 of its sessions have no fourth block; the 2021 cohort (C mice) ran 30 free choice trials per block, the Methods 20. The paper's code counts them with the others.

233 operant logs are byte-identical between the PPX and DREADD folders of the cognitive assay zip, and 75 between the A77636 and DREADD folders; they are the training logs and baseline sessions of mice used in two experiments, deposited twice. No drug or washout session is shared.

In the Zenodo workbook Data_ICD_FigS1_SNcTH_CellCounting_RawImages.xlsx, the Figure S1K&L sheet labels two blocks 'Session1_Park' (rows 35 and 118), the second presumably session 2 control, and two rows of the Figure S1D sheet (D3 and N4 at -3.51 mm) have their count and area columns shifted. The rotarod workbook has 40 control mice where Table 1 gives 31.

The Figure S6C legend and Table 1 give p < 0.01 for the CNO reduction of oIPSC amplitude by Wilcoxon signed-rank test in 6 cells, but a two-sided exact signed-rank test on 6 pairs cannot give less than p = 0.031, which is what the deposited values give.

In the CNO open field zip of the Zenodo deposit, the files of mice H0 and H0.4 (H0_openField_CNO_061523.xlsx and H0.4_openField_CNO_061523.xlsx) hold identical velocity traces, one recording deposited under two mice. Twelve of the CNO files (2023 H and J mice other than H1 and J3) have no tracking gap starting 19.5 to 21 min, so nothing in them marks the injection.

Six of the 30 PPX parkinsonian mice with delay discounting sessions (C3.1, E3.3, E4, H4.1, N1, N5.1) have no entry in the striatal histology workbook, and two parkinsonian histology mice (E3, E3.2) are in no README list, so 24 mice can be matched for Figure 3 where the paper has 28. Whether E3.3 is E3 or E3.2 under another name cannot be told from the deposit.

Questions for the authors. (1) When was the drug injected in each open field file (A77636 and CNO)? This attempt assumed 20 min after the start, where most files lose tracking briefly. (2) Was striatal TH normalized to the control mice of each staining cohort or to all controls? The DMS loss is 56.8% one way and 52.4% the other. (3) Which test gives p = 0.03 for the PPX effect on K in Figure 1J? Dunn's comparison of baseline against PPX ON gives p = 0.19 here, the Friedman test over three conditions p = 0.032, while the same procedure reproduces the A77636 Dunn's p-values exactly. (4) Were the Bonferroni comparisons after the repeated measures one-way ANOVA of Figure S2I-K made on the pooled error (sphericity assumed) or by paired comparisons? With the pooled error, K and AUC differ from baseline after washout (p = 0.028 and 0.0072); with paired comparisons K does not (p = 0.063).

disagreements.reason: The Bonferroni comparisons by paired t tests are stated as an assumption, but are not the better-supported choice. The paper's printed p-values favour the pooled error: baseline against OFF is K p = 0.01 and AUC p < 0.01; pooled gives 0.028 and 0.0072, paired 0.063 and 0.039. Pooled matches the paper's significance pattern in all six Table 1 and legend comparisons and paired misses two. Paired is closer only on ON against OFF AUC (0.0011 against 0.0019; pooled 0.0051), and both are significant there. The record's case for paired rests only on Prism's guide, and icd.rm_oneway's docstring says the pooled comparisons are 'as GraphPad Prism makes them by default' and calls the paired tests 'Table 1's reading' without support. The verifier would record reproduced, with the pooled error as the stated assumption.

entries.description: Tests the findings of Zhuang, Lemak, Sridhar and Nelson (2025) on dandiset 001177 and on the paper's Zenodo deposit (doi:10.5281/zenodo.15258978). The dandiset holds raw voltage, LFP and threshold crossings of the striatal recordings, without sorted or labelled units, so the electrophysiology claims are blocked. The delay discounting, rotarod, open field, histology and slice claims are tested on the Zenodo files, recounting every operant session from its raw log.
